author: Karl Rock
description:
This is the reality of the massive second-hand clothing trade in parts of Pakistan. Mountains of discarded garments, often shipped from Western countries, end up in these bustling markets where everything is priced at a flat rate of just 17 cents.

You can find high-end brands like Zara sitting right in the middle of these piles. It is a surreal experience to spot a tag that says Made in Turkey while rummaging through dusty, stained fabric on the ground.

These markets are part of a complex global textile ecosystem. While it feels like a treasure hunt, the reality is grittier than it looks. Most of these clothes are unwashed, sometimes stained, and require a serious amount of cleaning before they could ever be worn.

It is a stark reminder of the fast fashion cycle, where clothes travel thousands of miles just to end up in a pile like this. Would you dig through this to find a deal?
title: 17¢ Shopping in Pakistan
